title: Sandtable Beacon
tagline: Pucks in a burning building hear the occupants' phones; each phone appears in the right room of a map built from the building's own data (record, aerial, 3D twin), drawn only as precisely as the measurement allows, and an AI command agent routes the rescue and writes the report.
abstract: When a commercial building is on fire, the incident commander's hardest question is who is still inside, and where. Sandtable Beacon is a command and reporting centre for that question. When the alarm comes in, an AI command agent reads three layers for the address (the building record with its tenants, the aerial image, the 3D twin) and writes the pre-incident plan. A crew then places small pucks (Qorvo DWM3001CDK boards: Bluetooth and UWB) in the building. Occupants who opened the opt-in app are ranged through their phones, and each phone is drawn as what the measurement supports: a ring, two candidate points, or one point, in the right room and beside the tenant the building record expects there. Phones without the app are only a device count. The agent prioritises, routes a rescue crew through the twin, issues the radio order, re-plans and writes the report the command post keeps. Sponsor layers run as labelled fixtures; positions are simulated until the boards run.
aha: Two pucks give each phone two possible places, mirror images of each other; the twin's walls rule one out, so phone 1 lands as a point in the dentist's office the building record expects to be full, while phone 2 honestly stays 'two places: search both'. The building's own data does the job of a third puck.
how_it_works: Pre-plan: a tool-using agent reads the building record (CoStar layer), the aerial image (Vexcel layer, through a vision tool) and the 3D twin (Matterport layer)
Pucks in: DWM3001CDK boards on stock firmware, positions tape-measured and clicked onto the plan; opt-in iPhones range them and report status (lane L16's Beacon module)
Drawn honestly: one puck a ring, two pucks two candidates, the twin deletes impossible ones, a point only for a fix; no app means a device count, never people
Accountability: the record's tenants and expected occupancy per suite set against the phones heard, as ranges
Command: the agent prioritises, routes a crew through the twin, radios the order, re-routes when a phone's geometry improves, requests EMS
Report and feeds: a printable command-post report, GeoJSON and Cursor-on-Target
stack: Claude via the Anthropic SDK, the Claude CLI, or replay of recorded real runs (claude-sonnet-5-5 recordings)
Lane L16 Beacon module (vendor/beacon): locator, tracker, simulator, iOS app (Apple Nearby Interaction)
Qorvo DWM3001CDK on stock Nearby Interaction firmware
Bench uwb-kit (vendor/uwbkit) for the simulated Crews mode
Scout radar simulator and DSP adapted from lane L08
Public open data: LA County assessor and LARIAC, City of LA business listings and GeoHub, US Census TIGERweb, USDA NAIP

sponsor_tech.costar: Building record: tenants by suite and floor, business category (life hazards inferred), available space, construction, stories, sprinklers; drives who-is-expected-where in the accountability table (the record against what the phones report) and the agent's pre-plan. Public repository: stand-in record from real public data for another building. Ran live and privately on Nov 14 2026 from the CoStar hackathon data kit (26 property fields, 72 current tenant rows, 18 available spaces for one building); docs/LIVE_STATUS.md, docs/TOOLKIT_SWAP.md.
sponsor_tech.matterport: 3D twin: rooms, walls, doors, walking graph; routes the crew and prunes impossible phone candidates (outside the outline, inside a wall). Public repository: synthetic interior fitted to a real footprint. Ran live and privately on Nov 14 2026 through the Model API on a scanned suite (8 rooms with real boundaries, 48 walls, 14 doorways, 30 scan positions) with the Showcase SDK view embedded and steered on localhost.
sponsor_tech.vexcel: Aerial: the sides of the building, approach, staging, hydrants, roof; the agent looks at the image through a vision tool. Public repository: real USDA NAIP imagery. Ran live and privately on Nov 14 2026 through the Vexcel API v2 (a 3 to 6 cm ortho, roof, four obliques; the vision tool counted parking stalls on them).
sponsor_tech.anthropic: Claude as the command agent (tool use in a plan, act, re-plan loop); the hands-free demo replays recorded real responses; the live private run used the Claude CLI backend end to end (pre-plan, five situation turns, after-action report, 0 fallbacks); the API-key backend is written and not exercised (no key on the build machine).

left_hardware: 1. (Lane L16) Bring up the two DWM3001CDK pucks and the iPhone app with the Beacon module: follow vendor/beacon/hardware/BRINGUP.md (lane L16's guide, vendored; flashing in vendor/beacon/hardware/FLASH.md, the iOS app in vendor/beacon/docs/IOS_BUILD.md). Works when http://localhost:1885/healthz answers with source 'pucks'.

2. Start this board next to it (about 2 min): python -m sandtable.demo --beacon-url http://localhost:1885 (Windows: .venv\Scripts\python -m sandtable.demo --beacon-url http://localhost:1885). Works when the board at http://localhost:1810/ shows the Beacon badge as connected and not SIM.

3. Tape-measure the two pucks from two walls of the demo room, click 'Place pucks' and click them onto the room plan (fine-tune the metres in the dialog). Works when P1 and P2 show on the plan as 'placed by hand'.

4. Open the occupant app on the two iPhones. Works when each phone appears as two rings crossing at two points; where the twin's walls remove the mirror point it becomes a fix, otherwise the board says it cannot choose.

5. Click 'Dispatch alarm' before step 4 so the agent has the pre-plan; with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set and LLM_BACKEND=anthropic the agent decides live, otherwise the labelled fallback policy routes the crew.
6. Optional: the crew phone page http://localhost:1810/crew.html?unit=RIT on the Android phone (adb reverse tcp:1810 tcp:1810).
7. No hardware for Scout (radar) or Crews (tags): both run simulated only on these boards.

Tape-measured positions of the two pucks in the demo room, and which room of the twin the demo room stands in for

rubric.Use of the data (30%): Record says who should be in each suite; twin gives rooms, routes and deletes impossible phone positions (two pucks become one point); aerial gives sides, approach and staging read by a vision tool; combined into 'phone B1, Suite 310, dentists, patients may be sedated, 17 m from Stair B'.
rubric.Agentic depth (30%): Situations as goals with a reply budget; the agent chooses tools (record, aerial vision, twin, phones, accountability) and ends in actions (assign with route, radio, EMS request, observations, record corrections); must search a ring or two candidates, never 'go to the phone'; re-called when geometry improves. Beacon turns use the labelled fallback policy until recorded.
rubric.Usefulness (25%): Incident commander and command post: who is inside, where, who is unaccounted for as an honest range, and a report at the end; prevention bureaus get a pre-plan draft for any commercial address.
rubric.Demo and polish (15%): One screen, two physical pucks and two iPhones, a printable report, a phone page for the rescue team that reads the feed; every uncertain thing drawn as uncertain.

limitations: No phone and no puck has been in the loop of any number reported; the live path (stock Qorvo firmware, lane L16's iOS app) is written, and the real range error of an iPhone against these boards is unmeasured

Opt-in only: a phone without the app is never ranged or identified; the most a puck could give is a Bluetooth device count, and devices are not people; the app must stay open with the screen on as built
Two pucks often leave two candidates; the twin removes one only when the geometry allows

The public repository runs on stand-in data for all three sponsor layers (real public data and NAIP imagery for a different building, a synthetic interior whose walls are plausible, not surveyed). With the owner's keys and the CoStar data kit the same code ran live and privately on Nov 14 2026 on one real Los Angeles office building (CoStar record, a Matterport scan of one suite, Vexcel imagery); none of that data is published, the scan covers one suite, and its georeference is about 94 m from the record's point (flagged, not corrected)
Expected head counts and life hazards are estimates and inferences from the record

Agent turns in the hands-free demo are replays of recorded real model runs (beacon, scout and mayday scripts: every turn replayed, 0 fallbacks, results/replay_check_*_auto_3A2T.json); anything outside the recorded scene runs on a live model when one is configured, otherwise on a labelled deterministic policy that always finishes the exercise
Scout (radar) and Crews (tags) are simulation-only on these boards; the radar simulator was written alongside its detector

owner_questions.q: [Phones] Can a UWB board range a victim's phone over UWB at all?
owner_questions.a: Yes, with exactly your boards: a Qorvo DWM3001CDK running Qorvo's stock Nearby Interaction firmware ranges an iPhone 11 or later through Apple's accessory protocol, once the person has opened our app. Both your iPhones give distance (about 60 readings a second); neither gives direction to an accessory. The app reads the distance and reports it; the board itself only logs it on its debug channel.

owner_questions.q: [Phones] Can it be done cold, to a phone whose owner installed nothing?
owner_questions.a: No. An iPhone's UWB radio only answers a session started by an app with the user's permission. Cold, a radio can only count Bluetooth advertisements nearby: a rough band of devices by signal strength, no identity, and devices are not people. The stock puck firmware cannot even do that; the UNO Q's own radio can (written, never run).

owner_questions.q: [Phones] One puck or two for angle?
owner_questions.a: One puck gives a ring. Two give two candidate points, mirror images across the line between the pucks; the twin's walls often delete one. Three pucks not in a line give a position. The phone's own direction would turn one ring into a point, but an iPhone 14 or 15 does not report direction to an accessory without camera assistance (a moving phone that can see), so do not count on it. Simulated numbers follow when the evaluation finishes.

owner_questions.q: [Phones] Will the phone keep answering with the screen off?
owner_questions.a: Not as built tonight: keep the app open (it keeps the screen awake). Two ways exist and are not built: a Bluetooth-paired background session in which only the puck gets the measurements, and, on iOS 18.4 or later, a Live Activity that lets the app keep ranging.

owner_questions.q: [Phones] Can we put both UWB boards on one device we throw in?
owner_questions.a: It works poorly. Bearing from two single-antenna boards comes from the difference of two ranges: at 10 cm spacing it is useless, at 30 cm about 14 to 38 degrees of error, at 50 cm about 8 to 23 degrees, and the mirror ambiguity remains. Simulated numbers follow.

owner_questions.q: [Phones] Or one puck on the Android phone and one on the UNO Q, two separately powered pucks?
owner_questions.a: Two separate pucks a few metres apart are far better than two boards on one device: tens of centimetres, with two candidates that the twin can often cut to one. The Android phone is only worth using as a power source: the stock firmware prints nothing a phone could read. Recommended for the live demo: three separate pucks on battery banks, 2 to 3 m apart, not in a line; the UNO Q can power one and run the server.

Power only (5 V on either micro-USB port). The range comes back through the iPhone app over Wi-Fi. Stand the board upright, at least 15 cm off the floor, component-free side toward the phone. Puck positions are measured with a tape and clicked onto the plan: the stock firmware cannot range board to board.

owner_questions.q: [Radar] Is one UWB sensor enough to scan a room?
owner_questions.a: No. A single DWM3001CDK board cannot hear its own echoes. Qorvo's own staff say the module cannot transmit and receive at the same time. The smallest radar is two boards: one transmits, the other records the echoes that arrive after the direct pulse.

Its antenna is switched either to the transmitter or to the receiver. One frame lasts at least 32.6 µs, but a wall 3 m away answers after 20 ns, while the board is still transmitting. The receiver only switches on after the frame ends, by which time every room echo has already passed.

owner_questions.q: [Radar] How do multiple boards fix it?
owner_questions.a: One board transmits and the others listen. Each pair turns an echo's delay into an ellipse with the two boards as foci. More boards give more ellipses at different angles, and the target sits where they cross. The boards first range each other to learn their own positions, because every ellipse needs known foci.

owner_questions.q: [Radar] How many are needed, and what does each added board buy?
owner_questions.a: Two boards give presence and breathing but no position. Three give a 2-D position (3 ellipses), four add a redundant check (6), and five add better angles and outlier rejection (10). In the sample throw, the area that fits every pair shrinks from 4.01 m² (two boards) to 0.40 m² (three) and 0.15 m² (five).

owner_questions.q: [Radar] What is the 'map', and what is it not?
owner_questions.a: It is a coarse echo map: a few strong reflectors, a rough outline, what moved, and where the room disagrees with the stored twin. It is not a LiDAR-grade model, because echoes about 0.3 to 0.6 m apart merge and walls reflect like mirrors. The twin is the map; the boards add people, breathing and changes.

owner_questions.q: [Radar] Why does this beat cameras and LiDAR in smoke, and where does it not?
owner_questions.a: Smoke particles (0.01 to 1 µm) scatter light and LiDAR strongly but are negligible to a 46 mm radio wave. In fire tests, LiDAR erred below 4 m visibility while radar stayed within 1%. Thermal imagers also see through smoke and remain better at seeing fire. Flames, wet walls and metal cost radio signal; a still, non-breathing person stays invisible.

owner_questions.q: [Radar] What is the biggest open risk?
owner_questions.a: Signal strength. The sample victim's echoes arrive 25 to 36 dB below the direct pulse. In real recorded data, the empty room's own multipath already flickers at about 22 dB below. Expect detection within a few metres of the pucks. A breathing person across a 9.5 m room is unproven until measured.

All of the radar. No board has run it, and the reused echo-reading firmware targets ESP32 boards, not the DWM3001CDK. Scout is a secondary, simulation-only mode of Sandtable Beacon. The timing and geometry arithmetic is exact; detection performance is not measured. On the one real recording available, the reused tracker followed clutter, not the person.
